source.name: ASTRA physics spread set
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: The time period of a simple pendulum of length L on Earth is T. On a planet where g is four times that on Earth, the period becomes
questions.explanation: T = 2π√(L/g). If g → 4g, T → T/2.

questions.stem: For a particle in SHM, the acceleration is maximum when the displacement from the mean position is
questions.explanation: a = −ω²x, so |a| is largest at extreme displacement.

questions.stem: The phase difference between displacement and velocity in SHM is
questions.explanation: v = ω√(A² − x²); velocity leads displacement by π/2.

questions.stem: A spring of force constant k is cut into two equal parts. The force constant of each part is
questions.explanation: For series halves, each has length L/2 so k' = 2k.

questions.stem: In damped oscillations, the amplitude decreases exponentially with time because of
questions.explanation: Friction/viscous drag remove energy, so amplitude decays.

questions.stem: The rms speed of oxygen molecules at temperature T is v. At temperature 4T it becomes
questions.explanation: v_rms ∝ √T, so at 4T the rms speed is 2v.

questions.stem: According to the kinetic theory of gases, the absolute temperature of an ideal gas is proportional to the
questions.explanation: (1/2)m⟨v²⟩ = (3/2)kT for translational KE.

questions.stem: The pressure exerted by an ideal gas is proportional to
options: square of mean speed of molecules
root mean square of reciprocal speeds
questions.explanation: P = (1/3)ρ⟨v²⟩, so P ∝ mean square speed.

questions.stem: The degrees of freedom for a diatomic gas molecule at room temperature (ignoring vibration) is
questions.explanation: 3 translational + 2 rotational = 5.

questions.stem: Mean free path of gas molecules is inversely proportional to
options: square of molecular diameter and number density
questions.explanation: λ = 1/(√2 π d² n), so λ ∝ 1/(d² n).

questions.stem: In an n-type semiconductor, the majority charge carriers are
questions.explanation: Donor impurities provide extra electrons as majority carriers.

questions.stem: A p-n junction diode is forward biased when
options: p-side is connected to negative and n-side to positive of the battery
p-side is connected to positive and n-side to negative of the battery
both sides are at the same potential
questions.explanation: Forward bias: p positive, n negative relative to each other.

questions.stem: The output of a NOT gate is HIGH when its input is
questions.explanation: NOT inverts: Y = Ā.

questions.stem: Zener diodes are primarily used as
questions.explanation: In reverse breakdown they hold nearly constant voltage.

questions.stem: In a common-emitter transistor amplifier, the phase difference between input and output signals is
questions.explanation: CE amplifier inverts the signal (180° phase shift).

questions.stem: In an isothermal process for an ideal gas, the change in internal energy is
questions.explanation: U depends only on T for an ideal gas; ΔT = 0 ⇒ ΔU = 0.

questions.stem: First law of thermodynamics is a statement of conservation of
questions.explanation: ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW expresses energy conservation.

questions.stem: For an adiabatic process on an ideal gas, which relation is correct?
questions.explanation: Adiabatic: TV^(γ−1) = constant (also PV^γ = constant).

questions.stem: The efficiency of a Carnot engine operating between 327°C and 27°C is
In a cyclic process, the change in internal energy of the system is
questions.explanation: State function U returns to its initial value after a cycle.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the four fundamental forces?
questions.explanation: Friction is electromagnetic in origin, not a fundamental force.

questions.stem: A hypothesis becomes a scientific theory when it
options: is proposed by a famous scientist
questions.explanation: Theories rest on extensive experimental support.

questions.stem: The unification of electricity and magnetism was largely due to the work of
questions.explanation: Maxwell’s equations unify electric and magnetic fields.

questions.stem: Conservation laws in physics are closely linked to
questions.explanation: Noether’s theorem links symmetries to conserved quantities.

questions.stem: The coefficient of linear expansion α and volume expansion γ for an isotropic solid are related by
questions.explanation: For isotropic solids, γ = 3α.

questions.stem: Newton’s law of cooling states that the rate of heat loss is proportional to
options: the absolute temperature of the body
the excess temperature of the body over surroundings
the square of the absolute temperature
questions.explanation: dθ/dt ∝ (θ − θ0) for moderate excess temperatures.

questions.stem: Latent heat of vaporisation is the heat required to
options: raise temperature of unit mass by 1°C
change unit mass from liquid to vapour at constant temperature
change unit mass from solid to vapour directly
questions.explanation: L_v is heat for liquid ↔ vapour phase change at boiling point.

questions.stem: Among copper, water and air (typical values), the best conductor of heat is
questions.explanation: Metals like copper have very high thermal conductivity.

questions.stem: A bimetallic strip bends on heating because the two metals have different
questions.explanation: Unequal expansion causes curvature of the strip.

questions.stem: Faraday’s law states that induced emf is equal to the negative rate of change of
questions.explanation: ε = −dΦ_B/dt.

questions.stem: Lenz’s law is a consequence of conservation of
questions.explanation: Induced current opposes the change, consistent with energy conservation.

questions.stem: The SI unit of self-inductance is the
questions.explanation: L is measured in henry (H).

questions.stem: Eddy currents can be reduced by using
questions.explanation: Lamination increases resistance path and cuts eddy losses.

questions.stem: Mutual inductance between two coils depends on
options: relative orientation and number of turns
only the resistance of the wires
only the frequency of AC used
questions.explanation: M depends on geometry, orientation, turns, and core.

questions.stem: Electromagnetic waves are produced by
questions.explanation: Accelerating charges radiate EM waves.

questions.stem: In free space, the speed of EM waves is
In an electromagnetic wave, the electric and magnetic fields are
options: perpendicular and out of phase by π/2
questions.explanation: E ⊥ B and both are perpendicular to propagation; they are in phase in plane waves.

questions.stem: Which has the longest wavelength among the following?
questions.explanation: Among the listed, microwaves have the longest wavelength.

questions.stem: The ozone layer is important because it absorbs
questions.explanation: Stratospheric ozone strongly absorbs harmful UV.

questions.stem: In the photoelectric effect, the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons depends on
options: frequency of light and work function
only the wavelength of light, not the metal
questions.explanation: K_max = hν − φ.

questions.stem: de Broglie wavelength of a particle of momentum p is
questions.explanation: λ = h/p.

questions.stem: Increasing the intensity of incident light in a photoelectric experiment increases the
options: number of photoelectrons emitted per second
questions.explanation: Intensity raises photon flux; stopping potential depends on frequency.

questions.stem: The work function of a metal is 2 eV. The threshold frequency is (take h = 4.14 × 10^−15 eV s)
Davisson–Germer experiment confirmed
questions.explanation: Electron diffraction from a crystal showed de Broglie waves.

questions.stem: The bandwidth required for amplitude modulation with message bandwidth fm is about
questions.explanation: AM DSB needs roughly twice the message bandwidth.

questions.stem: Sky-wave propagation relies mainly on reflection from the
questions.explanation: HF sky waves bounce off ionospheric layers.

questions.stem: In space-wave propagation, the signals travel essentially
options: in a straight line in the troposphere / LOS
questions.explanation: Space/LOS waves travel nearly in straight lines (TV, microwave links).

questions.stem: The process of recovering the original message signal from a modulated wave is called
questions.explanation: Demodulation (detection) extracts the baseband message.

questions.stem: Moment of inertia of a thin ring of mass M and radius R about its central axis perpendicular to its plane is
questions.explanation: All mass is at distance R: I = MR².

questions.stem: Torque is equal to the rate of change of
questions.explanation: τ = dL/dt.

questions.stem: A rigid body is in pure rolling without slipping when
questions.explanation: No slip: v_cm = ωR for a wheel of radius R.

questions.stem: The centre of mass of a uniform triangular lamina lies at the
questions.explanation: For a uniform triangle, CM coincides with the centroid.

questions.stem: By the parallel-axis theorem, I = I_cm + Md². Here d is the distance between
options: any two points on the body
the CM axis and a parallel axis
questions.explanation: d separates the CM axis from the parallel axis of interest.

questions.stem: In Bohr’s model, the angular momentum of an electron in the nth orbit is
questions.explanation: L = nħ = nh/2π.

questions.stem: The spectral series of hydrogen that lies in the visible region is the
questions.explanation: Balmer transitions (to n=2) fall in the visible.

questions.stem: Rutherford’s alpha-scattering experiment concluded that
options: most of the atom’s mass and positive charge is in a tiny nucleus
electrons are in definite orbits only
questions.explanation: Large-angle scattering implied a compact positive nucleus.

questions.stem: The ionisation energy of hydrogen atom in the ground state is
questions.explanation: E1 = −13.6 eV; ionisation needs +13.6 eV.

questions.stem: In the Bohr model, the radius of the nth orbit is proportional to
questions.explanation: r_n = n² a0 for hydrogen.

questions.stem: If the percentage errors in measurement of mass and velocity are 2% and 3%, the percentage error in kinetic energy is
Dimensional formula of Planck’s constant is the same as that of
questions.explanation: h has dimensions of angular momentum: ML²T⁻¹.

questions.stem: 1 light year is a unit of
questions.explanation: A light year is the distance light travels in one year.

questions.stem: The number of significant figures in 6.022 × 10^23 is
questions.explanation: 6.022 has four significant figures.

questions.stem: For a projectile launched with speed u at angle θ on level ground, the maximum height is
questions.explanation: H = (u sinθ)² / (2g).

questions.stem: The horizontal range of a projectile is maximum when the angle of projection is
questions.explanation: R = u² sin2θ / g is max at θ = 45°.

questions.stem: In uniform circular motion, the centripetal acceleration is directed
questions.explanation: a = v²/r radially inward.

questions.stem: Two vectors of equal magnitude A have a resultant of magnitude A. The angle between them is
questions.explanation: |R|² = 2A²(1+cosθ) = A² ⇒ cosθ = −1/2 ⇒ θ = 120°.

questions.stem: The relative velocity of A with respect to B is
questions.explanation: v_AB = v_A − v_B by definition.

questions.stem: Stress is defined as
questions.explanation: Stress = F/A.

questions.stem: The breaking stress of a wire depends on
questions.explanation: Ultimate strength is a material property.

questions.stem: Shear modulus is the ratio of
questions.explanation: η = shear stress / shear strain.

questions.stem: Elastic potential energy density stored in a stretched wire is
questions.explanation: u = (1/2) × stress × strain.

questions.stem: Pascal’s law states that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is
questions.explanation: Hydraulic machines rely on undiminished pressure transmission.

questions.stem: Bernoulli’s equation is a statement of conservation of
questions.explanation: It equates mechanical energy per unit volume along a streamline.

questions.stem: The excess pressure inside a soap bubble of radius R and surface tension T is
questions.explanation: Soap bubble has two surfaces: ΔP = 4T/R.

questions.stem: Terminal velocity of a small sphere falling in a viscous fluid is proportional to
questions.explanation: Stokes: v_t ∝ r² (for given densities and η).

questions.stem: Archimedes’ principle states that the buoyant force equals the
questions.explanation: Buoyancy = weight of displaced fluid.

questions.stem: Magnetic susceptibility χ for a diamagnetic substance is
questions.explanation: Diamagnets have χ slightly negative.

questions.stem: The magnetic meridian at a place is
options: the vertical plane containing the Earth’s magnetic axis direction
questions.explanation: Magnetic meridian is the vertical plane through B_H.

questions.stem: Curie temperature is the temperature above which a ferromagnetic material becomes
questions.explanation: Above T_C, spontaneous magnetisation vanishes → paramagnetic.

questions.stem: The SI unit of magnetic field strength H is
questions.explanation: H is measured in A m⁻¹.

questions.stem: In a series LCR circuit, resonance occurs when
questions.explanation: At resonance XL = XC so X = 0 and Z = R.

questions.stem: Average power consumed in a pure capacitor over a full AC cycle is
questions.explanation: Current leads voltage by 90°; average power is zero.

questions.stem: Quality factor Q of a series LCR circuit is
An ideal transformer cannot change
questions.explanation: Ideal transformer conserves power: VpIp = VsIs.

questions.stem: Binding energy per nucleon is maximum for nuclei near
questions.explanation: Stability peaks near ⁵⁶Fe.

questions.stem: In beta-minus decay, the mass number A of the nucleus
questions.explanation: n → p + e⁻ + ν̄; A unchanged, Z increases by 1.

questions.stem: The activity of a radioactive sample after two half-lives becomes
questions.explanation: Each half-life halves activity: after 2 → 1/4.

questions.stem: Nuclear fission is typically initiated in reactors by
questions.explanation: Slow neutrons efficiently induce fission in ²³⁵U.

questions.stem: Mass defect is converted into binding energy according to
questions.explanation: Einstein’s E = mc² relates mass defect to BE.

questions.stem: Acceleration due to gravity at height h (h ≪ R) above Earth’s surface is approximately
questions.explanation: g(h) ≈ g(1 − 2h/R) for h ≪ R.

questions.stem: Escape speed from Earth’s surface is
questions.explanation: v_esc = √(2GM/R) = √(2gR).

questions.stem: Kepler’s second law is a consequence of conservation of
questions.explanation: Equal areas in equal times follow from central-force angular momentum conservation.

questions.stem: Gravitational potential at a distance r from a point mass M is
questions.explanation: V = −GM/r (zero at infinity).

questions.stem: Orbital speed of a satellite in a circular orbit of radius r about Earth is
questions.explanation: Centripetal requirement: v = √(GM/r).

questions.stem: In Young’s double-slit experiment, fringe width β is
questions.explanation: β = λD/d.

questions.stem: Brewster’s law states that tan ip equals
questions.explanation: tan ip = μ (relative refractive index).

questions.stem: For constructive interference in a thin soap film in reflected light (near normal incidence), 2μt equals
questions.explanation: Extra π phase from front reflection ⇒ bright for 2μt = (n+1/2)λ.

questions.stem: The resolving power of a telescope is increased by increasing the
questions.explanation: RP ∝ D/λ; larger objective aperture helps.

questions.stem: Huygens’ principle is used to explain
questions.explanation: Secondary wavelets explain reflection, refraction and diffraction qualitatively.

questions.stem: Electric potential due to a point charge q at distance r is
questions.explanation: V = q/(4πε0r).

questions.stem: Capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor with plate area A and separation d (vacuum) is
questions.explanation: C = ε0A/d.

Energy stored in a capacitor is
Inserting a dielectric of constant K between plates of an isolated charged capacitor
questions.explanation: C → KC; Q fixed ⇒ V = Q/C decreases.

questions.stem: Force on a charge q moving with velocity v in magnetic field B is
questions.explanation: F = q(v × B).

questions.stem: Magnetic field at the centre of a current-carrying circular loop of radius R is
questions.explanation: B = μ0I/(2R) at the centre.

questions.stem: A charged particle moving parallel to a uniform magnetic field experiences
Ampere’s circuital law relates ∮ B·dl to
questions.explanation: ∮ B·dl = μ0 I_enclosed (magnetostatics).

questions.explanation: Perpendicular B gives uniform circular motion (constant speed).
